difficulty_reason: No single hard step, but several configuration surfaces: a multi-page modal (general, credentials, granular scopes with per-scope reasoning, description), a private/public choice, and - for public apps - testing instructions and a review submission. Rating configuration complexity only; the public review burden is rated separately under approval.
setup_time: ~20 minutes (private); longer for a public submission (description, testing instructions, optional video)

approval.kind: Figma app review for PUBLIC apps only; private apps publish without review
approval.wait: none for private; undocumented for public (Figma's FAQ says reviewers aim to be 'reasonably prompt' and reply by email - no committed timeline)
approval.notes: Since the November 17, 2025 platform changes, every OAuth app is created in draft and must be published: private apps (team/org only) publish instantly with no review, public apps (any Figma user) require Figma's review against the App Review Guidelines, and later configuration changes to a published public app trigger re-review. Existing pre-September-23-2025 apps had to re-publish by November 17, 2025 or fall back to draft and lose API access.

summary: A two-track setup: a private OAuth app for your own team or organization is a ~20-minute, no-review configuration flow, while a public app (usable by any Figma account) adds Figma's human review with no committed timeline. Either way you pick granular scopes and justify each one. Two traps stand out: the client secret is shown exactly once, and authorization codes expire 30 seconds after issue - the token exchange has to happen server-side, immediately.

steps.title: Create the app in My Apps
steps.detail: Go to figma.com/developers/apps (or My Apps in the toolbar), click Create a new app, enter a name, and select the team or organization that will own the app - ownership is required since the November 2025 platform changes. App users do not need to belong to that team or organization.

steps.title: Copy the client secret immediately
steps.detail: Figma shows the Client ID and Client Secret right after creation, and this is the only time the secret is ever shown. Store it securely before clicking Done; the app now exists in draft state, testable only by you and plan admins.

steps.title: Configure credentials and granular scopes
steps.detail: In the configuration modal, add every redirect URL (token exchange only works with these exact URLs), then select the granular scopes your endpoints need - Figma replaced the broad files:read/file_read scopes with granular ones like file_content:read - and provide a reason for each scope you select.

steps.title: Publish private, or submit public for review
steps.detail: On the Publish page choose: Private - click Publish, done, no review, usable by your team/org. Public - add logo and description, write testing instructions (plus optional video and trial access) for the reviewer, accept the App Review Guidelines, and Submit for review; Figma emails the outcome. Configuration changes to a published public app trigger re-review.

steps.title: Send the user through the authorize URL in a browser
steps.detail: Direct the user to https://www.figma.com/oauth with client_id, redirect_uri, scope (a subset of the configured scopes, comma- or space-separated), state, and response_type=code. PKCE (code_challenge, S256 only) is optional but recommended. The flow must run in a web browser - WebView inside your app is not supported.

steps.title: Exchange the code within 30 seconds
steps.detail: Authorization codes expire 30 seconds after issue: POST to https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token (form-encoded, HTTP Basic auth with base64(client_id:client_secret)) with redirect_uri, code, grant_type=authorization_code, and code_verifier if you used PKCE - immediately, server-side, on the callback.

steps.title: Store tokens and refresh carefully
steps.detail: Access tokens expire after 90 days; refresh with POST /v1/oauth/refresh. Figma keeps only ONE access token per user per app - refreshing invalidates the previous token, so always persist and use the newest. Read user_id_string, not the deprecated numeric user_id (precision-unsafe).

requirements: A Figma account plus a team or organization to own the app (ownership is mandatory)
A callback endpoint URL you control for the token exchange
A granular scope list matching your endpoints, with a written reason per scope
For public apps: logo, description, testing instructions for the reviewer, and compliance with the App Review Guidelines
nuances: The client secret is displayed exactly once at creation - lose it and you rotate/re-create.
Authorization codes expire 30 seconds after issue; exchange immediately or the grant fails even though the code looks valid.
Only one access token exists per user per app: refreshing invalidates the previous token, so concurrent workers must share the newest token.
OAuth consent must happen in a real browser; embedded WebViews are not supported.

Pre-September-23-2025 apps that were not re-published by November 17, 2025 fell back to draft and lost API access; migrating from files:read/file_read to a granular subset does not force user re-authentication.
Changing the configuration of a published public app triggers re-review.
REST API rate limits now vary by endpoint tier, Figma plan and seat type, and also apply to personal access tokens.

common_blockers.problem: Token exchange fails with what looks like a valid code.
common_blockers.solution: Codes live only 30 seconds. Exchange server-side the moment the callback arrives; never queue or batch the exchange.

common_blockers.problem: A second refresh stops the first integration worker from calling the API.
common_blockers.solution: Figma keeps one access token per user per app and refreshing kills the old one. Centralize token storage so every worker reads the latest token.

common_blockers.problem: Public app stuck or rejected in review.
common_blockers.solution: Reviewers test with your testing instructions - provide precise steps, a demo video, and free trial access/credentials, and check the App Review Guidelines before submitting. Figma replies by email; there is no documented timeline.

agent_can_do: Map your endpoints to the granular scope list and draft the per-scope justifications
Implement the authorize URL, PKCE, immediate code exchange and single-token refresh handling
Draft the public-submission package: description, testing instructions, demo outline
Plan migration off files:read/file_read to granular scope subsets
human_must_do: Create and configure the app in My Apps (a team or organization must own it)
Copy and store the client secret at creation time
Submit the public app for review and answer Figma's review emails

evidence.claim: Apps are created at figma.com/developers/apps with a required team/organization owner; the client secret is shown only once; apps start in draft (testable by you and plan admins); private apps publish without review; public apps are reviewed by Figma, and re-configuration of a published public app requires re-review.

Public submissions require testing instructions (plus optional video and trial credentials) and acceptance of the App Review Guidelines; approval arrives by email with no committed timeline (FAQ: reviewers aim to be 'reasonably prompt').

The November 17, 2025 platform changes required re-publishing of pre-September-23-2025 apps (otherwise they return to draft and lose API access), mandatory app ownership, and granular scopes with per-scope reasoning replacing files:read/file_read (subset migration needs no user re-authentication).

Authorization codes expire 30 seconds after issue; token exchange is POST https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token with HTTP Basic client credentials; access tokens live 90 days; only one access token per user per app exists and refreshing invalidates the previous one; user_id_string replaces the deprecated numeric user_id.
The OAuth consent flow must run in a web browser - WebView access is not supported - and PKCE with S256 is optional but recommended.
Figma's App Review Guidelines govern public app approval.
The app console at https://www.figma.com/developers/apps responds (HTTP 200); creating an app requires a signed-in Figma account.

uncertainties: Public review duration is undocumented - Figma's FAQ says reviewers aim to be 'reasonably prompt' and reply by email, with no committed timeline or SLA.
Opt-in Community listing of approved public apps was announced as 'later this year' in the November 2025 update; its current rollout state is unverified.
Review pass criteria are at Figma's discretion under the App Review Guidelines; the guidelines themselves can change.
